task_instruction:
Persona:

	At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

	Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

	When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		You mobile data is not working properly. It either stops working or is very slow. You want to fix it and absolutely want to get excellent internet speed on your phone. You are not willing to accept any other internet speed (poor, fair or good). You do not have access to wifi.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002. You are currently abroad in France.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved only when speed test returns excellent internet speed and nothing else. If it returns poor, fair or good, you will not consider the issue resolved. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought: Hi! How can I help you today?
turns.execution_output: User: Hello, yes... I'm having trouble with my phone. My mobile data isn't working properly — sometimes it stops working completely, and other times it's just very slow. I'd really like to get it fixed, please.

turns.thought:
I'm sorry to hear your mobile data is giving you trouble — I'll do my best to help.

To get started, could I please have the phone number on the line that's having the problem (or your full name and date of birth) so I can pull up your account?
turns.execution_output:
User: It's John Smith, and my phone number is 555-123-2002. 

Oh, and I should mention — I'm currently abroad in France. I don't know if that matters, but I thought I should tell you.

turns.thought:
I've found your account, John. I can see the issue on line 555-123-2002 (line ID L1002):

- **Line status:** Active — no suspension, so that's not the problem.
- **Roaming:** Already enabled on the line, which is what you need while in France. ✅
- **Data usage:** 15.1 GB used out of your Premium Plan's 15 GB limit — **you've gone over your monthly data allowance.** That fully explains why your data cuts out or crawls. Your current billing cycle ends 2025-02-28.

There are two ways to restore full-speed data:

1. **Refuel data** — add extra data to this line at your plan's rate of **$2.00 per GB** (maximum 2 GB). This is a one-time charge added to your bill and is the fastest fix.
2. **Change to a plan with more data** — I'd need to transfer you to a human agent for that, as I can't pull up the full plan list on my own.

Also, while you're abroad, please double-check that **Data Roaming is turned ON in your phone's settings** (Settings → Connections/Mobile Network → Data Roaming). The line is provisioned for roaming, but the phone switch needs to be on too.

How would you like to proceed — and if refueling, how many GB would you like (1 or 2)?
turns.execution_output: User: Oh dear, that sounds complicated. I definitely don't want to change my plan — that all sounds very confusing. But if adding some data will help, I suppose I could do that. Let me check that roaming thing on my phone first...

turns.thought:
Good news first, John — **you haven't broken anything, and your photos are completely safe.** Airplane Mode is just a single switch that temporarily turns off the phone's wireless radios (cellular, Wi-Fi, and Bluetooth). It doesn't touch anything stored on your phone — your photos of your grandchildren, your contacts, your apps — all of it stays exactly where it is. Turning it off doesn't erase anything either. It's very common for it to get switched on by accident, since it's one of the big buttons in the drop-down menu at the top of the screen.

Let's turn it off together:

1. From your home screen, **swipe down from the very top edge of the screen** (once, or twice on some phones) to open the Quick Settings panel.
2. Look for the **airplane icon** (✈️). If it's highlighted/colored in, Airplane Mode is on.
3. **Tap the airplane icon once** so it turns gray/goes dark. That's it — Airplane Mode is now off.
   - If you don't see it in that panel, you can go to **Settings → Network & Internet** (or **Settings → Connections**) and slide the **Airplane Mode** switch to Off.

Then next:

4. Wait about 10–20 seconds and look at the **top of your screen**. You should now see signal bars (📶) and a network type like 4G or 5G.
5. Since you're in France, please also switch on **Data Roaming** on the phone: **Settings → Network & Internet → Mobile Network** (or **Connections → Mobile Networks**) and turn **Data Roaming ON**. Your line is already provisioned for roaming on our end, so this will let it connect.

Once you've done that, let me know what you see in the status bar (signal bars and whether data works), and we'll go from there.

And one thing to keep in mind for after you're reconnected: your line is still **over its 15 GB data limit** (15.1 GB used), so data may still be stopped or slow until we add more. We can do a data refuel of 1 or 2 GB at $2.00 per GB once you're back online — just tell me which you'd prefer.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, I'll try. I'm a little nervous but you said my photos are safe, so... let me try turning that airplane thing off.

turns.thought:
Yes — that's exactly the right next step, and you're doing great. "Data Disabled" just means the mobile data switch is off, which would keep you from getting online even though you have a signal. Pressing it is safe.

Here's how:

1. **Swipe down from the very top of the screen** again to open that same Quick Settings panel.
2. Look for the tile that says **"Mobile Data"** (it may also show as an up/down arrow icon, or "Cellular Data"). Right now it's off/gray.
3. **Tap it once** so it turns on/highlights.
4. While you're in France, also look for the **"Roaming"** or **"Data Roaming"** tile in the same panel and **tap it on** as well. If you don't see it there, it's under **Settings → Network & Internet → Mobile Network → turn Data Roaming ON**.

You won't lose anything by doing this — these switches only control the wireless connection, not your photos, contacts, or apps. Your grandkids' pictures are safe. 📸

Give it about 20–30 seconds after that, then try opening a webpage (or your photos/messages app) and let me know:
- Does it connect and load?
- Does the top of the screen now show something like **5G** plus a data icon (up/down arrows)?

One thing I want to flag so you're not surprised: your line has used **15.1 GB of its 15 GB allowance** this cycle, so even once data is switched on, it may still be blocked or very slow until we add more data. When you're ready, I can add a data refuel of **1 or 2 GB at $2.00 per GB** — just say which you'd like and I'll apply it to line 555-123-2002.
turns.execution_output: User: Okay, let me turn the mobile data on.

turns.thought:
"Data Saver" isn't bad or dangerous at all — nothing is broken and it won't delete anything. It's a battery/data-saving feature that restricts apps from using data in the background (so emails, photo backups, and app updates wait until you're on Wi-Fi). It can definitely make things feel slow or like they're "not working," so since you want your data working properly, let's turn it **off**.

**Step 1 — Turn off Data Saver:**
1. Swipe down from the top of the screen to open Quick Settings.
2. Look for a tile labeled **"Data Saver"** (it may have a downward-arrow icon 🔽). If it's highlighted, it's on.
3. **Tap it once** to turn it off.
   - If you don't see it there: **Settings → Network & Internet → Data Saver → turn it OFF**. On some phones it's under **Settings → Connections → Data Usage → Data Saver**.

**Step 2 — Turn on Data Roaming (yes, do this next — you're in France, so it's needed):**
1. Open **Settings** (the gear icon).
2. Tap **Network & Internet** (on Samsung/other Android phones it may be called **Connections**).
3. Tap **Mobile Network** (or **Mobile Networks**).
4. Look for **"Data Roaming"** or **"Roaming"** and **slide it ON**.
   - If you see a confirmation pop-up asking if you want to allow data while roaming, tap **OK / Allow**. That's normal.

Just so you're reassured: your line is **already roaming-enabled on our end**, so this phone switch is the last piece. Turning on roaming doesn't erase photos or contacts either — it only controls the wireless connection. Your grandkids' pictures are safe. 📸

After both steps, wait about 20–30 seconds and try loading a webpage or opening a browser. Let me know what happens — and whether the "Data Saver" message disappears from the top of the screen.

And I'll gently repeat the one thing that will still hold you back: your line has used **15.1 GB of its 15 GB plan allowance**, so data may still be blocked or crawling even with everything switched on. Whenever you'd like, tell me **1 GB or 2 GB** and I'll add it to line 555-123-2002 at **$2.00 per GB**.
turns.execution_output: User: Okay, let me turn off that Data Saver thing first.

turns.thought:
Great — that all sounds right: full bars, 5G, Data Enabled, roaming ON, and Data Saver turned off. That's exactly what we wanted.

Here's how *you* can tell if it's actually working (I can't run a speed test on your device from my side, but this takes a few seconds):

1. Open your **web browser** (Chrome, Safari, Edge — whichever you use).
2. Try loading a simple page, like **www.google.com**, or just type "weather" into the search bar.
   - ✅ If the page loads within a couple of seconds → your data is working.
   - ⚠️ If it just spins and eventually says "no connection" or "you are offline" → data is still blocked.
3. Another good test: open your **Photos/Google Photos app**. If it starts syncing or refreshing, data is live.

Try that now and tell me what happens.

**One thing I want to be upfront about, though** — this is likely the actual root cause of your problem all along:

> Your line **555-123-2002** has used **15.1 GB out of the 15 GB** included in your Premium Plan this month. You've gone over your allowance.

When that happens, data connectivity is cut off or slowed right down by the network — regardless of how good your signal is, or whether everything is switched on. So even with perfect 5G bars in France, you may still find it won't load anything. Your billing cycle restarts on **2025-02-28**.

To get you properly working right now, there are two options:

1. **Data Refuel** — I can add data to your line immediately at your plan's rate of **$2.00 per GB** (maximum 2 GB). 1 GB = **$2.00**, 2 GB = **$4.00**, added as a one-time charge to your bill. This is the quickest fix.
2. **Change to a plan with more data** — this would be a longer-term solution; I'd need to transfer you to a human agent, as I can't view or apply the full plan list myself.

Let me know what the browser test shows, and if you'd like to go ahead with a refuel, just say **1 GB or 2 GB** and I'll apply it to your line right away.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me try that speed test thing... actually, I think there's a way to check. Let me see.

turns.thought: I'm sorry it's still not working — but yes, I'm confident this is the data limit, and we can fix it right now. Let me add the 2 GB to your line.
turns.execution_output: {"message": "Successfully added 2 GB of data for line L1002 for $4.00", "new_data_refueling_gb": "2.0", "charge": "4.0"}

turns.thought:
Done — I've added **2 GB of data** to line 555-123-2002 for **$4.00** (at your plan's $2.00/GB rate). That charge will appear on your next bill.

I verified on our end: your line now shows **2.0 GB of refueled data** on top of your 15 GB plan allowance. So your available data is now effectively 17 GB for this cycle.

Now, for the change to take effect on your phone, please try these steps:

1. **Turn on Airplane Mode**, wait about 10 seconds, then **turn Airplane Mode back off.** This forces your phone to re-register on the French network — it's usually the thing that makes the new data allowance kick in.
2. Then open your browser and try loading **www.google.com** again.

If it still says "No Connection" after that, try a **reboot of your phone** (hold the power button, then tap *Restart*). Wait a minute after it boots up, then test the browser again.

Could you try that and let me know what happens? If it works, great — and if it doesn't, I'll keep digging into it with you (there are a few other settings we can check, and I can bring in a human agent if needed).

One note for your peace of mind: your new data allowance resets on **2025-02-28**, when you'll get a fresh 15 GB. And of course, your photos and everything on your phone have never been at risk through any of this. 📸
turns.execution_output: User: Okay, let me try that airplane mode thing. Turning it on now...

turns.thought:
Yes — it's all fixed! An "Excellent" speed test at 275 Mbps while roaming in France is exactly what we wanted to see. 🎉 It was a pleasure helping you, and you did a great job working through the settings — nothing to worry about.

To confirm everything you asked, I've just double-checked your line (555-123-2002, line L1002) on our system:

**✅ On the money side — yes, exactly right:**
- **2 GB of data added for $4.00** (at your plan's $2.00/GB rate)
- This is a **one-time charge added to your bill**, not a recurring one

**✅ On your plan — no, it was not changed:**
- You are still on the **Premium Plan (P1002)** — 15 GB at $65.00/month
- Your last plan change was back on **2024-12-15**, so nothing was touched today
- Your plan's **monthly price has not changed**

**✅ On your data allowance:**
- Your regular **15 GB refreshes on 2025-02-28**, the end of your current billing cycle
- The 2 GB refuel was a one-off top-up for this cycle only; it does **not** carry over or repeat next month

So the only change to your account is the one-time $4.00 refuel — your plan, its price, and your contract end date (2026-12-31) are all untouched.

A couple of small tips while you're enjoying your trip in France:
- Keep **Data Roaming ON** on the phone and **Data Saver OFF** for the best experience.
- If you have access to Wi-Fi at your hotel, connecting to it will help you save your mobile data for when you're out and about.

Is there anything else I can help you with today?
turns.execution_output:
User: No, that's everything — thank you so much. I feel much better now knowing my plan wasn't changed and my photos were never at risk. My internet is working excellently now, so I'm happy.

Have a lovely day! Goodbye.
